cards.back: Biguanide for type 2 diabetes. Lowers liver glucose output. Side effects: diarrhoea, lactic acidosis
Sulfonylurea. Closes K-ATP channels so beta cells release insulin. Risk of hypoglycaemia
Long-acting insulin analogue given once a day
Thiazolidinedione. Activates PPAR-gamma and improves insulin sensitivity. Causes fluid retention
DPP-4 inhibitor. Increases incretin levels and raises insulin release after meals
SGLT2 inhibitor. Blocks glucose reabsorption in the kidney tubule so glucose is lost in urine
ACE inhibitor for hypertension. Side effects: dry cough, hyperkalaemia, angioedema
ACE inhibitor. Prodrug converted to enalaprilat in the liver
Angiotensin receptor blocker. No cough. Avoid in pregnancy
Dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker. Vasodilator. Causes ankle oedema
Non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker. Slows the heart rate. Causes constipation
Beta-1 selective beta blocker. Reduces heart rate and contractility
Non-selective beta blocker. Avoid in asthma
Beta-1 selective beta blocker cleared by the kidney
Loop diuretic. Blocks the Na-K-2Cl transporter in the loop of Henle. Causes hypokalaemia and ototoxicity
Thiazide diuretic. Acts on the distal tubule. Can cause hyponatraemia and raise calcium
Aldosterone antagonist, a potassium-sparing diuretic. Gynaecomastia is a side effect
Inhibits the Na-K ATPase pump. Narrow therapeutic index. Toxicity causes nausea and yellow vision
Class III antiarrhythmic. Can cause thyroid and lung toxicity
Vitamin K antagonist. Monitor with INR. Reversal with vitamin K
Activates antithrombin. Monitor with aPTT. Reversal with protamine
Direct factor Xa inhibitor, an oral anticoagulant
Irreversibly inhibits COX-1 and COX-2, so platelets cannot make thromboxane
P2Y12 antagonist that prevents platelet aggregation
Statin. Inhibits HMG-CoA reductase and lowers LDL cholesterol. Can cause myopathy
Blocks cholesterol absorption in the gut
Penicillin. Beta-lactam antibiotic that inhibits cell wall synthesis. Allergy is a risk
Fluoroquinolone that inhibits DNA gyrase. Risk of tendon rupture
Aminoglycoside that binds the 30S ribosome. Nephrotoxic and ototoxic
Tetracycline. Inhibits the 30S ribosome. Avoid in pregnancy and children
Macrolide that inhibits the 50S ribosome. Can prolong the QT interval
Glycopeptide active against MRSA. Red man syndrome if infused too fast
Active against anaerobes and protozoa. Avoid alcohol
Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, used for urinary tract infection
Azole antifungal that inhibits ergosterol synthesis
Guanosine analogue that inhibits viral DNA polymerase, used for herpes
Short-acting beta-2 agonist. Relieves bronchospasm in asthma. Tremor and tachycardia
Long-acting beta-2 agonist, never used alone in asthma
Inhaled corticosteroid for asthma prevention. Oral thrush is a side effect
Oral corticosteroid. Long-term use causes osteoporosis, hyperglycaemia and adrenal suppression
Antimuscarinic bronchodilator used in COPD
Proton pump inhibitor. Irreversibly blocks the H+/K+ ATPase in parietal cells
H2 receptor antagonist that reduces gastric acid
5-HT3 antagonist antiemetic. Can prolong the QT interval
Opioid agonist in the gut that slows motility and treats diarrhoea
Opioid agonist at mu receptors. Side effects: respiratory depression, constipation. Reversed by naloxone
Opioid antagonist used for overdose
Analgesic and antipyretic. Overdose damages the liver. Antidote is acetylcysteine
NSAID that inhibits COX. Risk of gastric ulcers and kidney injury
SSRI antidepressant. Blocks serotonin reuptake. Risk of serotonin syndrome
Tricyclic antidepressant. Overdose causes arrhythmias. Anticholinergic effects
Mood stabiliser. Narrow therapeutic index. Toxicity causes tremor. Monitor levels
Typical antipsychotic that blocks D2 receptors. Extrapyramidal side effects
Benzodiazepine that enhances GABA-A. Dependence and sedation. Reversed by flumazenil
Anticonvulsant that blocks sodium channels. Induces liver enzymes
Anticonvulsant with zero-order kinetics. Gingival hyperplasia
Thyroid hormone replacement for hypothyroidism
